s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with fever and vomiting
salient_findings: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
key_facts: 18-hour history of symptoms
Fever of 39 °C
Vomiting
Constipation
Unremarkable past medical history
Normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
Normal prothrombin time, INR, glucose, creatinine, urea, sodium, and potassium
Elevated C-reactive protein at 134.5 mg/L
Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness on examination
Soft stool without blood on digital rectal examination
Normal chest examination
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on erect abdominal radiograph
Dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph
5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness and elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on erect abdominal radiograph

shortlist.label: Mesenteric adenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein and abdominal tenderness

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic condition that could present with acute abdominal pain and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Perforated viscus
shortlist.why_kept: Rigid abdomen and elevated C-reactive protein, although no free air on imaging

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT, although less likely given age and presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography, along with air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph, is highly suggestive of intussusception, which is a condition where a part of the intestine telescopes into another part.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: The location of the mass is not typical for appendicitis, and the presence of air–fluid levels in the small bowel is more suggestive of intussusception.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: Meckel's diverticulitis typically presents with a more localized area of tenderness and may have a different appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While small bowel obstruction can cause similar symptoms, the presence of a distinct mass on imaging is more suggestive of intussusception.

rejected.label: Mesenteric adenitis
rejected.why: Mesenteric adenitis typically presents with more diffuse abdominal tenderness and may not have a distinct mass on imaging.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: Inflammatory bowel disease typically has a more chronic course and may not present with a distinct mass on imaging.

rejected.label: Perforated viscus
rejected.why: Perforated viscus would likely present with more severe symptoms and signs of peritonitis, and the imaging findings would be more consistent with free air and fluid.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma is less likely in a child with acute symptoms and would not typically present with the specific imaging findings seen in this case.
